answer: Mesa Deposit Curve. Each new agent identity posts a refundable deposit that scales with its cluster's recent identity growth; the mesa widens sharply past a threshold, so ten fresh agents cost far more per head than the first. Honest agents recover the deposit on clean exit, while attackers forfeit it if flagged. Reference nodes, marked like a lotus in the registry, set the curve slope. Forfeit is jade-hard: 30% of deposit slashed per confirmed duplication.
